thought.text: Even the base DN isn't found now — the image's own bootstrap ldif must have failed too. Let me check the root DSE and try to diagnose.

reasoning_content:
Something's off. The base DN `dc=example,dc=org` is returning "No such object" — but in previous attempts, the naming context existed. Wait, could it be that in this new bootstrap, the base DN wasn't created at all? Let me check the root DSE.

No wait — this is a new bootstrap. "Add image bootstrap ldif..." should have added the base DN (from 03-base-dn.ldif or a similar file). But now the base DN returns "No such object". That means the image's bootstrap ldif (01-config-password, 02-security, 03-base-dn...) also failed!

Why? The image's bootstrap ldif files also use `sed -i` (01-config-password.ldif uses `sed -i` to replace LDAP_CONFIG_PASSWORD_ENCRYPTED). These are in the image's own directory `.../bootstrap/ldif` (not a subdirectory). They should be on writable image filesystem...

Wait, but I'm mounting `.ddev/ldap-seed` at `.../bootstrap/ldif/custom` — just a subdirectory, so the parent should be writable.

Hmm, but `ldapadd` is silent (debug level). Let me check the actual result. Maybe `dpkg-reconfigure slapd` created the base DN via `slapd/domain string example.org`. In that case, the naming context should exist...

Let me check the root DSE's namingContexts and try a base search on dc=example,dc=org.

action.command: su - dev -c 'cd /workspace && export PATH=$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH && echo "=== rootDSE namingContexts ==="; docker exec ddev-tfm-fachplanung-openldap ldapsearch -x -H ldap://localhost -b "" -s base "(objectClass=*)" namingContexts 2>&1; echo "=== base DN search ==="; docker exec ddev-tfm-fachplanung-openldap ldapsearch -x -H ldap://localhost -b "dc=example,dc=org" -s base "(objectClass=*)" dn 2>&1 | grep -E "^dn|^result"; echo "=== try admin bind ==="; docker exec ddev-tfm-fachplanung-openldap ldapwhoami -x -H ldap://localhost -D "cn=admin,dc=example,dc=org" -w admin 2>&1'
